extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, and funders studying or designing peer review systems (publication and grant review)
extracted.subtask_description: Systematic taxonomy and evaluation of bias types in peer review (publication and grant), methodological approaches to studying bias, critiques of the literature, reform alternatives, and implications for designing less-biased rubrics and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognitive cronyism / particularism
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer favors proposals using their own theoretical/methodological commitments (Travis & Collins 1991).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies a reviewer preference for work aligned with their intellectual commitments; assess whether decisions systematically advantage work matching reviewers' approaches rather than objective merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliative bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer favors institutions/networks they belong to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for systematic positive outcomes when institutional or network ties exist between reviewer and applicant/author; includes in-group preferences based on affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer favors their own subfield.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect whether reviewers give higher assessments to work within their sub-discipline and lower to interdisciplinary or outside-subfield work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservatism
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer favors incremental over revolutionary work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure penalties against high-risk/high-reward or paradigm-challenging proposals; consider how emphasis on safe, incremental contributions may bias outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Male applicants/authors favored (Wennerås & Wold 1997, Bornmann et al. 2007).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine gender-based disparities in review outcomes; control for productivity and other legitimate quality signals when attributing effects to bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Race/ethnicity bias
rubrics_metrics.description: White applicants/authors favored (Ginther 2011, Erosheva 2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze outcomes by race/ethnicity, accounting for field, institution, and other covariates to detect systemic favoritism or disadvantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Favoring applicants from 'central' vs 'peripheral' countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether reviewers systematically prefer applicants from economically or reputationally central countries over peripheral ones; consider language and infrastructural confounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional prestige bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Favoring elite institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate whether affiliation with prestigious institutions yields higher success independent of proposal quality; audit historical decisions and control for applicant merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career stage bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Favoring established vs early-career researchers (or vice versa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect systematic advantages/disadvantages tied to career stage; consider how criteria may implicitly favor experience or novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Favoring native English speakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for lowered evaluations linked to non-native language use even when substantive quality is comparable; separate language fluency effects from content quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalizing high-risk innovative work (Boudreau 2016).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure reduced success rates for novel or unconventional proposals; consider whether evaluation criteria undervalue innovation relative to safe contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Favoring quantitative over qualitative or vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify systematic preferences for particular methods; evaluate whether methods-incompatible criteria lead to uneven assessments across valid methodological approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Favoring fashionable over unfashionable topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect whether trendy or currently popular research topics receive disproportionate positive evaluations compared to less fashionable but meritorious topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Favoring positive over null results (especially in publication review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess selection pressure for statistically significant/positive findings in publication decisions; consider how this skews the literature and evaluative rubrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer-applicant assignment bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-random matching introduces systematic effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine how assignment procedures (matching by topic, affiliation, prior co-authorship, etc.) create systematic advantages or disadvantages; randomization tests can reveal assignment-based bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halo effect from prior funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Past success predicts current success regardless of merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit whether prior awards or endorsements unduly influence current evaluations; distinguish reputation effects from current-proposal quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anchoring
rubrics_metrics.description: First reviewer's score influences later reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for ordering effects and the influence of initial scores or comments on subsequent evaluations; consider blinding or independent scoring to mitigate anchoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group dynamic bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel deliberation amplifies dominant voices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how deliberation processes privilege assertive panel members or majority views, potentially drowning out minority perspectives; examine facilitation and decision rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical approach to studying bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Test for systematic effects in real review data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use observational or experimental analysis of actual review outcomes to detect patterns consistent with bias; requires careful controls and specification of counterfactuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological approach to studying bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Study how the review process produces variable outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze process features (assignment, scoring scales, deliberation) and how they generate variance or systematic patterns; can reveal structural sources of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normative approach to studying bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine what SHOULD count as bias versus legitimate quality judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify conceptual boundaries and ethical/policy judgments about which differences are unjust prejudice versus reasonable evaluative distinctions; necessary for designing remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual confusion in bias literature
rubrics_metrics.description: "Bias" used to mean different things in different studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require explicit definitions of bias in studies and rubrics; avoid conflating disagreement, taste, or legitimate quality signals with bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistent operationalization
rubrics_metrics.description: What counts as 'the same proposal' varies across studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardize operational definitions and comparison units when measuring bias; inconsistent operationalization undermines comparability of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underspecification of the counterfactual
rubrics_metrics.description: Unclear what unbiased review would produce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the counterfactual carefully (e.g., blind review, randomized assignment) when claiming bias; design studies to approximate the unbiased scenario.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty separating bias from disagreement
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers disagree, it's hard to know which is 'biased'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish epistemic disagreement from systematic prejudice by using controls, replication, and external benchmarks; avoid labeling all disagreement as bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind review
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymize authors and reviewers to reduce identity-based biases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use author anonymization to mitigate gender, race, institution, and nationality biases; effectiveness depends on how easily identities can be inferred from content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open review
rubrics_metrics.description: Make reviewer identities public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase transparency and accountability by disclosing reviewer names; consider trade-offs such as reviewer willingness to be candid or potential reputational pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Community judgment after dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shift selection and evaluation to the broader community post-dissemination; can democratize review but may replicate popularity biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lottery-based allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Randomization removes individual bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lotteries (often applied to short-listed proposals) to reduce idiosyncratic reviewer effects; preserves some fairness but may leave merit assessment less determinative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic decision aids
rubrics_metrics.description: Structured decision support tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ algorithms or structured rubrics to standardize evaluation; monitor for biases embedded in algorithms and ensure transparency and validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity in reviewer panels
rubrics_metrics.description: Heterogeneous panels reduce monoculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble reviewers with varied backgrounds/methodologies to counteract groupthink and disciplinary monocultures; combine with process safeguards to ensure diverse voices influence outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define operationally what 'bias' means
rubrics_metrics.description: A rubric that aspires to be unbiased must define operationally what 'bias' means in its context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit definitions for bias types relevant to the rubric's domain (e.g., gender, institution, method); this is prerequisite to measurement and remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit historical decisions for each bias type
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit historical decisions for each bias type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct retrospective analyses of prior reviews to detect patterns consistent with the taxonomy; use audits to inform targeted reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish legitimate quality differences from unjust prejudice
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that some 'biases' reflect legitimate quality differences vs. unjust prejudice — rubric must distinguish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build criteria and benchmarks that separate substantive quality signals from artifacts of identity or process; incorporate external standards where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build in structural protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Build in structural protections (anonymization, randomization, diverse panels) that don't depend on individual reviewer awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design process-level safeguards into rubrics and workflows so fairness does not rely solely on reviewers' good faith; combine multiple protections to address different bias types.
